Benchmarking Metrics | Renewed Rubric (7 → 12)

Two metric clusters, equally weighted for now. The original seven capture what companies built (architecture state); five new metrics (8, 9, 10, 11, 12) capture how they work (operating model, definition mechanism & enablers) — closing the gap between product-tech outcomes and the Lean PD Ops scope. Metric 9 carries two facets (9a, 9b); Metric 11 is a qualitative lens. Rubric bars are fixed before research, so every rating stays comparable.

Cluster A — What They Built  (existing 7, unchanged)
1. Platform ReuseSystemic reuse of physical assets across programs
2. ModularityDecoupled, recombinable module architecture
3. Configuration MgmtGovernance of variants & product definition
4. HW–SW IntegrationFusion of hardware & software domains
5. SDV MaturitySoftware-defined vehicle capability
6. OTAOver-the-air update breadth & cadence
7. Integrated ServicesMonetizable connected-service ecosystem
Cluster B — How They Work  (new operating-model & enabler metrics)
METRIC 8Speed / Time-to-ValueNEW

Elapsed time from concept freeze to Start-of-Production (SOP), plus how much of validation is virtual vs. physical-prototype-dependent. Measures how fast the PD system converts intent into producible value.

Leader
<24 mo concept-to-SOP; virtual-first validation (>60% simulation)
Strong
24–36 mo; heavy simulation use; disciplined process
Emerging
36–48 mo; mixed physical/virtual validation
Lagging
>48 mo; physical-prototype-dependent; serial
Why it matters →Directly quantifies speed-to-market. Benchmark disruptors reach ~21 months concept-to-pilot vs. up to ~48 months for legacy OEMs. Informed Decision Making
Expected Ford placement: Lagging / Emerging — serial, prototype-heavy cycles.
Source: McKinsey OEM development-cycle analyses; zonal-architecture studies (20–30% faster concept-to-mass-production).

REUSE TAXONOMY — per Valerdi (applies to Metric 9a)

AdoptedReused as-is, same application. No physical change, no re-validation. Highest-value reuse.
ManagedReused as-is, but a new application. No physical change, but requires context re-validation.
ModifiedPhysically changed for the new use. Real engineering effort & re-qualification.
Value hierarchy for scoring: Adopted > Managed > Modified > Net-new. A Leader maximizes Adopted + Managed and treats Modified / net-new as deliberate exceptions.
METRIC 9aPart Reuse / Carryover RatioNEW

Share of parts across the Valerdi states (Adopted / Managed / Modified / net-new), weighted toward as-is reuse. Measures how well the PD system avoids re-creating what already exists.

Leader
Majority Adopted + Managed reuse; net-new minimized; active part rationalization
Strong
Strong carryover; Modified used purposefully, not by default
Emerging
Some reuse; ad-hoc; Modified & net-new rising
Lagging
Defaults to Modified / net-new; little as-is reuse; proliferation
Why it matters →Maps directly to Ford's part-reuse mandate. As-is reuse (Adopted/Managed) is the cheapest path — every avoided net-new part removes design, tooling, and validation cost. Platform Thinking & Economies of Scale
Expected Ford placement: Lagging — "part-first" proliferation, weak carryover governance.
Source: McKinsey cost-of-complexity modeling (part standardization cut total cost ~3% despite higher unit cost); TNGA-class R&D-resource reduction of 20–30%.
Interpretation flag: the Adopted > Managed > Modified value ranking is my proposed mapping of Valerdi's taxonomy onto the tiers — open for the team to challenge before it locks.
METRIC 9bRework / Engineering-Change RateNEW

Volume and timing of engineering changes — especially late and post-SOP changes. High reuse means little if the reused content triggers constant downstream rework; this is the efficiency counter-check to 9a.

Leader
Low change volume; changes front-loaded; minimal late / post-SOP rework
Strong
Contained volume; disciplined, fast ECR process
Emerging
Moderate change latency; some late changes
Lagging
High rework; frequent late & post-SOP changes
Why it matters →The purest measure of redundancy in the PD process — late changes are the most expensive dollars in development, and the direct target of the engagement's savings case. Informed Decision Making
Expected Ford placement: Lagging / Emerging — "endless follow-ups," surrogate-driven late changes.
Source: McKinsey R&D-efficiency benchmarks (core levers yield 15–20% efficiency); digital-twin studies (reduced physical prototyping → up to ~12% EBIT).
METRIC 10Digital Thread / Single-Source-of-Truth MaturityNEW

Degree to which product definition — requirements → BOM → 3D → cost — lives in one connected, live, machine-readable model versus siloed static artifacts. The measurable form of "making the invisible visible."

Leader
Single live, data-centric model; digital twin; real-time cost/3D/part linkage
Strong
Integrated PLM backbone; most authoring connected & structured
Emerging
Partial integration; several authoring silos; manual reconciliation
Lagging
Document-centric; disconnected artifacts; tribal knowledge
Why it matters →This is Ford's core pain (44+ systems, 100+ disconnected artifacts) made measurable — and the direct target of a single governed PDL. Making the Invisible Visible
Expected Ford placement: Lagging — 8+ siloed authoring sources; document-centric culture.
Source: digital-twin EBIT uplift of up to ~12%; Gen-AI R&D productivity gains (30–70% on requirements/test work) — analyst & Tier-1 reported.
METRIC 11Transformation EnablersNEW · QUALITATIVE

What actually drove each transformation to succeed — not a performance score, but a coded archetype. Captured as one primary + secondary driver per company so Ford targets the real lever, not just the visible mechanism.

Leadership-Mandated
Top-down chief-engineer / exec conviction sets non-negotiable direction (e.g., Toyota CE model)
Capital / Finance-Forced
Platform economics & capex discipline force reuse (e.g., VW MQB business case)
Crisis / Burning Platform
Existential threat compels rapid, deep change (turnaround-driven)
Culture / Talent-Led
Software-native org & engineering culture enable it (e.g., Tesla, BYD)
Why it matters →Tells the COO which enabler moves the needle — if peers succeeded via leadership mandate, Ford's roadmap needs an executive owner, not just a new tool. Turns benchmarking into an actionable "how," not just "what." Purpose-Driven Innovation
Use for Ford: identify which enabler(s) Ford can credibly activate to de-risk the LPD roadmap.
Source: qualitative coding from company case studies & transformation literature; validated with Deloitte–Ford team (not a numeric benchmark).
Scope note: Metric 11 is the cross-cutting enabler lens (the “how the change was driven”). The scored instrument for Opportunity Area 6 — whether product definition is feature-structured — is Metric 12 below. The two are complementary, not duplicative.
METRIC 12Feature-Driven DefinitionNEW

Degree to which product definition is organized around customer-perceivable features/functions that carry through requirements → architecture → variant management, versus a “part-first” structure built on components and surrogates. Measures the mechanism behind Area 6 — not the software outcome (that is Metrics 5–6), but whether the PDL itself is feature-structured.

Leader
Feature model is the backbone of definition; features traced end-to-end; features monetized (OTA / feature-on-demand)
Strong
Formal feature-based PLE in place; most variants derived from a governed feature catalog
Emerging
Feature thinking in software only; hardware definition still part-first
Lagging
Part-first definition on static PDLs; features implicit; surrogate/clinic-driven
Why it matters →This is Area 6’s From→To (“part-first” → “feature-first”) made scoreable — and it is externally benchmarked: Gartner’s 2025 Digital Automaker Index ranks 24 OEMs on software-and-feature maturity, placing digital natives far ahead of legacy players and naming Ford among those needing to catch up. Purpose-Driven Innovation
Expected Ford placement: Lagging — part-first PDLs, feature intent captured via surveys/surrogates rather than a governed feature model.
Anchor (method, peer-reviewed): feature-driven systems-engineering procedure, Granrath et al., INCOSE Systems Engineering (Wiley), 2021. Named case: feature-based PLE at General Motors (BigLever / SPLC 2017 — vendor/academic). Cross-company placement: Gartner 2025 Digital Automaker Index; Wards Intelligence / Omdia SDV ranking; IMD Future Readiness Indicator 2025.
Confidence & overlap flag: the mechanism-specific, company-level evidence (GM feature-based PLE) is vendor/academic, not teardown — treat as Covered*, same tier as Areas 1&2. The Gartner/Wards/IMD rankings are independent-analyst but measure software-defined maturity, which overlaps Metrics 5–6; they are used here only to place Ford and confirm a leader/laggard spread, not as the definition-mechanism score itself.
Sourcing note (pre-COO): figures shown are external benchmark ranges from third-party analyses (McKinsey and comparable), deliberately chosen over less-audited OEM management claims. All are directional and flagged for joint Deloitte–Ford validation. Weighting: all quantitative metrics equally weighted at this stage; Metric 11 is a qualitative lens, not scored. Count: 7 original + 5 new (8, 9, 10, 11, 12) = 12 metrics; Metric 9 carries facets 9a & 9b.
